q8.answer: Counts live in one shared Redis, under the key rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}, one counter per customer per minute window. Each key gets EXPIRE 120 s when first created (count becomes 1), so old windows' keys remove themselves.

q9.answer: Budget resets at the fixed one-minute window boundary. windowStart = floor(redisTime/60)*60, so the next window uses a new key starting at 0. The old key just expires. It is a fixed window, not sliding, so a client can burst up to 2x across a boundary, which I accepted for v1.

q10.answer: The check-and-increment is a single Lua script (check_and_incr) run inside Redis. Redis runs scripts one at a time, so the read of the count, the count >= limit test and the INCR happen atomically. Two instances cannot both see 99 and both increment past 100.

q11.answer: Inside the Lua script, on a deny: retryAfter = max(1, windowStart + 60 - redisTime), in whole seconds, using Redis TIME. That is the time left until the current fixed window ends and the counter resets. It is returned to the gateway and sent as the Retry-After header.

q12.answer: No retry. On a Redis error or no answer within 50 ms, the gateway emits ratelimit_store_unavailable and forwards the request straight away (fail open). The client gets the normal backend response with no X-RateLimit-Limit or X-RateLimit-Remaining headers. A late Redis answer is ignored.
